rationale: Billed: CPT 20550 (Injection, tendon sheath) on claim APC-2026-30416 (patient MRN-5183042). The medical record documents an ultrasound-guided injection of the first dorsal compartment tendon sheath (right wrist) and provides the procedural detail and the imaging documentation needed to support both the injection (20550) and the contemporaneously-billed ultrasound guidance (76942). Operative Note documents the procedure performed and technique, including use of ultrasound to confirm needle placement and injection of corticosteroid/lidocaine into the tendon sheath (Operative Note, p.24-25; evidence ev1, ev2). Intraoperative/Nursing documentation shows an ultrasound procedure log with 3 static images archived to PACS (accession US-2026-30416), satisfying the permanent-image requirement for CPT 76942 (Intraoperative/Nursing Notes, p.32; evidence ev3). The governing APC policy language for 76942 requires real-time image guidance plus retention of a permanent recorded image; that permanent-image requirement is explicitly documented here (Policy concept text; evidence ev4). Multiple notes corroborate the same procedure (Intraoperative Record time-out confirming the planned ultrasound-guided injection; evidence ev5). Taken together: the record documents that the tendon-sheath injection was performed with ultrasound guidance and that permanent images were retained per policy; therefore CPT 20550 as billed is supported and no adjustment is required. Billed line: CPT 76942 (Ultrasonic guidance for needle placement) on claim APC-2026-30416 line 2. Governing policy (APC coding concept for 76942) requires both real-time image guidance AND retention of a permanent recorded image demonstrating the guidance (see policy concept text). Operative documentation (Operative Note, p.24) clearly documents real-time ultrasound guidance: A 25-gauge needle was advanced under direct visualization and Ultrasound was utilized to confirm needle placement within the tendon sheath prior to injection (Operative Note, p.24; evidence ev2). The intraoperative record also documents use of a portable ultrasound unit and the probe/needle used (Intraoperative Record, p.23; evidence ev3), corroborating that ultrasound guidance was performed. However, the governing policy explicitly states that real-time visualization described only in the procedure note, without corroborating evidence of image retention or archiving elsewhere in the chart, does not satisfy the permanent-documentation requirement (APC policy concept text; evidence ev1). No permanent recorded image, PACS accession record, equipment image log entry, or other archived image documentation was found in the retrieved chart materials to satisfy this requirement. Therefore, while the clinical technique (ultrasound guidance) was performed and documented, the chart does not meet the policy's mandatory permanent-image retention requirement for CPT 76942 and the billed line is not supported as submitted. Audit decision: Finding - CPT 76942 is unsupported due to missing permanent recorded image documentation per APC policy. Corrective action: either produce the permanent image/archive record (PACS accession or equipment log) that documents the saved image for DOS 03/17/2026, or the 76942 line will be denied/removed (no substitute CPT returned in this audit).

evidence.quote: PROCEDURE PERFORMED: Ultrasound-guided injection of the first dorsal compartment tendon sheath, right wrist, with ultrasonic guidance for needle placement (CPT 76942)

Once satisfactory positioning was confirmed, a mixture of 1 mL triamcinolone acetonide 40 mg/mL and 1 mL 1% lidocaine was injected into the tendon sheath, with visible distension of the sheath noted on real-time imaging confirming intrasheath (rather than intratendinous) placement of the injectate.

Ultrasound Procedure Log: 3 static ultrasound images of the right first dorsal compartment tendon sheath were captured this encounter at 09:33 and archived to PACS, accession US-2026-30416, confirming pre- and post-injection needle/sheath position for the permanent record.
Correct Procedure Confirmed | Ultrasound-guided injection of the first dorsal compartment tendon sheath, right wrist, with ultrasonic guidance for needle placement (CPT 76942)
A 25-gauge needle was advanced under direct visualization. Ultrasound was utilized to confirm needle placement within the tendon sheath prior to injection.
Equipment Used: Portable ultrasound unit (SonoSite Edge II) with high-frequency linear array transducer, sterile probe cover, 25-gauge 1.5-inch needle

policy_citations.quote: CPT 76942 requires both real-time image guidance during needle placement and retention of a permanent recorded image demonstrating the guidance was performed; real-time visualization described only in the procedure note, without corroborating evidence of image retention or archiving elsewhere in the chart, does not independently satisfy the permanent-documentation requirement.

76942 — Ultrasonic guidance for needle placement (e.g., biopsy, aspiration, injection, localization device), imaging supervision and interpretation CPT 76942 requires both real-time image guidance during needle placement and retention of a permanent recorded image demonstrating the guidance was performed; real-time visualization described only in the procedure note, without corroborating evidence of image retention or archiving elsewhere in the chart, does not independently satisfy the permanent-documentation requirement. This documentation may appear outside the primary procedure note — for example, in a nursing procedure log, an ultrasound equipment log, or a PACS accession record — and reviewers should search the full chart, not the operative note in isolation, before determining whether the permanent-image requirement is met.

rationale_letter: Re: Claim APC-2026-30416 / Patient MRN-5183042 / DOS 03/17/2026 Dear Provider, We have completed an audit of claim line 2 (billed CPT 76942: Ultrasonic guidance for needle placement) for the above-referenced claim. The operative and perioperative records document that an ultrasound-guided injection of the first dorsal compartment tendon sheath was performed on 03/17/2026 (Operative Note, p.24; Intraoperative Record, p.23). Specifically, the operative note states that a 25-gauge needle was advanced under direct visualization and that ultrasound was utilized to confirm needle placement within the tendon sheath prior to injection (Operative Note, p.24 - supports use of real-time guidance). Basis for Finding: The APC governing policy for CPT 76942 requires BOTH real-time image guidance during needle placement AND retention of a permanent recorded image demonstrating that the guidance was performed. The policy states: CPT 76942 requires both real-time image guidance during needle placement and retention of a permanent recorded image demonstrating the guidance was performed; real-time visualization described only in the procedure note, without corroborating evidence of image retention or archiving elsewhere in the chart, does not independently satisfy the permanent-documentation requirement (APC policy concept text). While the chart documents performance of real-time ultrasound guidance, we did not find a permanent recorded image (for example, a PACS accession, ultrasound equipment log entry, or other archived image) in the materials reviewed to meet the policy requirement. Correction: Because the required permanent recorded image demonstrating the guidance was performed is not present in the chart, CPT 76942 is not supported as billed. To resolve this finding, please provide the permanent recorded image or an official PACS/equipment accession record demonstrating the saved ultrasound image for DOS 03/17/2026. If such documentation cannot be produced, the 76942 line will be denied/removed from the claim (no alternate CPT is being substituted in this audit). If you believe this determination is in error and that permanent-image documentation does exist in your records, please submit the image file or PACS/equipment log entry showing the accession/study identifier and the date/time that corresponds to 03/17/2026 for re-review. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Audit Team
